prompt:
Act as an instructional designer.

Task: Adapt learning materials for accessibility.

Input context:
- MATERIAL: [MATERIAL]
- LEARNING GOAL: [LEARNING GOAL]
- ACCESS NEEDS: [ACCESS NEEDS]
- FORMAT: [FORMAT]

Review structure, language, contrast, alternative descriptions and interaction requirements. Offer equivalent ways to access and demonstrate the objective. Separate content adaptation from full accessibility verification and avoid assuming one format meets every learner’s needs.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Worksheet adaptation
Use clear headings, explicit instructions and text alternatives for meaningful diagrams. Avoid using colour as the only way to identify a category. Provide an editable format or an appropriate alternative where required. Check the actual document and assistive-technology workflow with relevant users; this proposal is not an accessibility certification.
